title: Pediatric Lupus Nephritis: ISN/RPS Classes, Induction and Targeted Therapies
subject: ss-paediatric-nephrology

steps.say: Renal involvement in juvenile systemic lupus is remarkably common and dictates long-term survival.
steps.tx: Assess pediatric patients early recognizing the high **Pediatric SLE renal involvement frequency** across clinical cohorts. Clinically evident renal involvement occurs in 50-80% of children with systemic lupus erythematosus, demonstrating substantially greater proliferative severity, higher rates of acute kidney injury, and accelerated progression compared with adult-onset disease.

vis.alt: Immune complex deposition causing malar rash and lupus nephritis.
vis.caption: Lupus: immune complexes injure skin and kidney together. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Standardized histological staging groups glomerular injury into six prognostic classes based on biopsy findings.
steps.tx: Classify renal tissue architecture utilizing the consensus **ISN/RPS pathological classification classes** on light microscopy. Histological categories comprise Class I (minimal mesangial), Class II (mesangial proliferative), Class III (focal proliferative < 50% glomeruli), Class IV (diffuse proliferative >= 50%), Class V (membranous), and Class VI (advanced sclerosing >= 90%), establishing the foundation for protocolized immunosuppression.

vis.alt: Microscopic patterns separating minimal change, FSGS, IgA and membranoproliferative disease.
vis.caption: Glomerular patterns that frame the lupus class. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Intensive induction therapy arrests severe proliferative immune injury to preserve surviving nephrons.
steps.tx: Initiate urgent immunosuppression following evidence-based **Class III/IV proliferative induction protocols** without delay. Proliferative induction therapy combines intravenous pulse methylprednisolone followed by high-dose oral corticosteroids with either mycophenolate mofetil at 1200 mg/m²/day or intravenous pulsed cyclophosphamide according to low-dose Euro-Lupus protocols, successfully achieving early disease remission in aggressive presentations.

nodes.label: Biopsy Confirmed Class III or IV LN
IV Pulse Methylprednisolone (10-30 mg/kg x 3 doses)
Oral Corticosteroids + MMF 1200 mg/m²/day or IV Cyclophosphamide

steps.say: Biologic add-on therapy enhances renal response rates while reducing toxic corticosteroid dependence.
steps.tx: Incorporate approved targeted biologics using **Belimumab add-on therapy** for refractory or active disease. Belimumab, an anti-BAFF/BLyS human monoclonal antibody, is approved as targeted add-on therapy for active lupus nephritis in children >= 5 years, binding soluble B-lymphocyte stimulator to improve primary renal response rates while significantly reducing maintenance corticosteroid exposure.

vis.title: Belimumab Monoclonal Antibody Specifications
rows: 10 mg/kg IV at weeks 0, 2, 4, then monthly
Reduces relapses and chronic organ damage

steps.say: The diagnostic pathognomonic hallmark on biopsy is intense multi-immunoglobulin and complement deposition.
steps.tx: Verify immune complex composition by demonstrating the pathognomonic **Full house immunofluorescence signature** under microscopy. Diagnostic renal immunofluorescence in pediatric lupus nephritis reveals intense granular full house staining positive for IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, and C1q deposited densely along the glomerular capillary walls and throughout the mesangial matrix, confirming systemic immune complex deposition.

vis.title: Glomerular Immunofluorescence Staining Profile
rows: Distinguishes SLE from pure post-infectious GN

steps.say: Serological markers correlate closely with histologic activity and warn of approaching relapses.
steps.tx: Track disease activity non-invasively through systematic **Anti-dsDNA and complement monitoring** at each visit. Proliferative inflammatory exacerbations correlate tightly with rising anti-dsDNA antibody titers and marked consumption of serum complement C3 and C4 components, signaling active complement activation in glomeruli and providing an early alert before overt worsening of clinical proteinuria occurs.

left.title: Active Proliferative Flare
points: Markedly elevated or rising anti-dsDNA titers
Depressed serum complement C3 and C4 levels
Active urine sediment with dysmorphic RBCs and casts

right.title: Serological Remission
points: Low, falling or negative anti-dsDNA titers
Normalization of both serum C3 and C4 levels

steps.say: Universal antimalarial coverage forms the essential background shield for all pediatric patients.
steps.tx: Prescribe disease-modifying therapy ensuring **Hydroxychloroquine baseline protection** is maintained continuously. Every child diagnosed with lupus nephritis must receive daily oral hydroxychloroquine at 3-5 mg/kg/day up to a maximum daily dose of 200-400 mg unless strictly contraindicated, providing vital protection against severe disease flares, arterial thrombosis, and progressive irreversible chronic renal damage.

vis.title: Hydroxychloroquine Baseline Therapy Parameters
rows: Inhibits endosomal TLR-7 and TLR-9 signalling
Improves lipid profiles and vascular compliance

steps.say: Maintenance therapy must be sustained over years to avoid debilitating relapses and graft loss.
steps.tx: Structure prolonged secondary prevention following the standard **Maintenance immunosuppression duration** guidelines. Following successful induction, maintenance immunosuppression with oral mycophenolate mofetil or azathioprine paired with low-dose oral prednisone must be sustained continuously for at least 3-5 years, preventing late nephritic relapses before any cautious dose taper is contemplated.

nodes.label: Oral MMF or Azathioprine + Low-Dose Prednisone
